title: Reduce safe guide-release selection to a directed feedback vertex set
statement: For one port per site, only pairwise permanent blocker edges i->j, no prerequisites and exact immediate product-preserving release, minimum distinct released guides equal minimum directed feedback-vertex-set size. Releasing i removes every edge sourced at i; a completion order exists iff the remaining graph is acyclic.

requires: Single fixed port, singleton blockers, no prerequisites and observed successful products.
A selected guide can be removed immediately without breaking the desired bond or leaving its steric footprint.
provides: For one port per site, only pairwise permanent blocker edges i->j, no prerequisites and exact immediate product-preserving release, minimum distinct released guides equal minimum directed feedback-vertex-set size. Releasing i removes every edge sourced at i; a completion order exists iff the remaining graph is acyclic.
assumptions: Release deletes outgoing footprint obstructions only; it does not reverse chemical precedence or acquire alternative ports.
costs: Minimum directed feedback vertex set/exact finite search plus all physical release and product-observation costs.
contract.units: Edges encode precedence j-before-i induced by product i blocking site j; cardinality counts distinct released guides.
contract.obstruction: Establish the exact pairwise/prerequisite-free interface before importing the graph reduction.

body: Every unreleased edge i->j requires j before i. A directed cycle of such edges makes these strict time inequalities impossible, so every cycle must contain a released source. Conversely, if released set R hits all directed cycles, deleting its outgoing edges leaves a DAG; any reverse topological order is feasible, releasing R immediately after each successful reaction. Cycles in this outgoing-deleted graph are exactly cycles avoiding R, so the minimum equals the usual directed feedback vertex set. This is a standard graph-theoretic reduction within the chemical model, not new graph theory. Additional chemical prerequisites can introduce opposite ordering constraints; multiple ports and cooperative blocking sets require the more general state search. The source-reported four-vertex4096-graph histogram is not independently replayed or accepted as a new numerical result.
